subject.title: fix(infra): make exec-approvals lock ownership filesystem-safe

question: Which open PR should be the canonical exec-approvals async-lock repair, and should it be required to provide exact-head filesystem runtime proof before merge?
rationale: Both open PRs target the same security-sensitive lock lifecycle, but neither an automated reviewer nor historical proof can choose the long-term branch or establish real behavior for its final head.

options.title: Use this rebased PR as canonical
options.body: Keep this branch and require a redacted exact-head VirtioFS run proving release, contention, and fail-closed behavior before merge.

options.title: Adopt the original candidate
options.body: Pause this PR and direct the original candidate at https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/111028 to rebase and provide exact-head proof instead.

options.title: Pause both candidates
options.body: Hold both PRs until the infra owner defines the desired shared-versus-local lock boundary and a single proof plan.

recommendation.title: Use this rebased PR as canonical
recommendation.body: Keep this branch and require a redacted exact-head VirtioFS run proving release, contention, and fail-closed behavior before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They own the detailed production reproduction and the original open candidate, so they are the best available technical routing contact for selecting and proving a canonical repair.
